properties.cost_note: Admission charged (members admitted free) but no price is published on the Society's pages.

properties.name: Mountain Elementary School (Gasquet)
properties.description: A small TK-8 open-enrolment magnet school in the redwoods of Gasquet, part of Del Norte County Unified and listed by CDE as an active public elementary school. The site states the TK-8 span and that it is a magnet school.
properties.source_note: Summarised from the official website; not a site visit.

properties.name: Nature River Trail (Jedediah Smith day-use area)
properties.description: A 0.6-mile accessible trail on compacted aggregate linking the day-use area and the campground through redwood forest with views of the Smith River. An accessible picnic area sits at the day-use trailhead, with accessible parking and restrooms near both ends.
properties.access_notes: State Parks: 0.6-mile accessible trail, compacted aggregate, generally flat; one armored crossing may be challenging in rain; accessible parking, restrooms and picnic area.
properties.source_note: Summarised from the official website; not a site visit.
properties.address: Trailheads in the Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park day-use area and campground, off US 199
properties.hours_note: Day use sunrise to sunset.
properties.cost_note: $8 per vehicle day-use fee at the campground entrance station.
properties.geo_source: official page: Google Maps directions link on https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=413 (park entrance)

trail_info.family_note: Stated accessible and generally flat; stroller-suitable by surface description (not stated by the park).
trail_info.warnings: Armored crossing can be difficult during rain. Dogs not allowed on trails.

properties.name: Northcoast Marine Mammal Center
properties.description: A nonprofit seal and sea lion rescue and rehabilitation center in Beachfront Park near the lighthouse, with outdoor animal pens, a harbor seal pup room and a gift shop/information center. Its stated aim includes public education about marine mammals, and it runs on donations and memberships.
properties.source_note: Summarised from the official website; not a site visit.
properties.address: 424 Howe Dr., Crescent City, CA 95531 (in Beachfront Park)
properties.hours_note: Only gift-shop winter hours are posted: Thu 1-4, Fri-Sat 11-4. Whether animal areas are open to viewing is not stated; call first.
properties.cost_note: No admission fee listed; donations requested.
properties.geo_source: OSM Nominatim geocode of the official street address '424 Howe Dr., Crescent City' (amenity), logged at ingest

properties.name: Ocean World
properties.description: A small private aquarium on US 101 at the south end of town offering a guided tour of roughly 45 minutes that includes a touch tide pool, a shark and bat-ray tank, resident seals and sea lions, and a sea-lion show. Tours leave about every 20 minutes and are first come, first served.
properties.access_notes: No accessibility statement on the official site; call to ask.
properties.source_note: Summarised from the official website; not a site visit.
properties.address: 304 Highway 101 South, Crescent City, CA 95531
properties.hours_note: Open daily; gift shop 9:00 am-6:00 pm, tours 9:15 am-4:30 pm, last tour varies with natural light; call ahead for late-day tours.
properties.cost_note: Ages 12 and over $16.95; ages 3-11 $10.95; 2 and under free (as listed on the official site).

properties.name: Panther Flat Picnic Area and swimming holes (Smith River NRA)
properties.description: A no-fee day-use picnic area next to the Panther Flat campground on the Middle Fork Smith River, with eight picnic tables, grills, water and a horseshoe pit. Two short paths lead from the picnic area to river swimming holes, one with a small sandy beach.
properties.access_notes: Page says 'Accessible sites available' and notes accessible flush toilets for the campground; not stated for the picnic area.
properties.source_note: Summarised from the official website; not a site visit.
properties.address: US 199, 2.5 miles east of the Gasquet visitor center
properties.hours_note: Campground open all year.
properties.cost_note: Picnic area is 'no-fee, day-use only'; campground charges separately.

properties.name: Pelican State Beach
properties.description: California's northernmost beach, a small undeveloped and secluded state beach right at the Oregon border with parking, beach access and surf-watching. There are no facilities, and the page recommends layered clothing for changeable weather.
properties.source_note: Summarised from the official website; not a site visit.
properties.address: US Highway 101 N at Gilbert Way, Smith River, CA (21 miles north of Crescent City)
properties.hours_note: Page says 'call park' for hours.
properties.cost_note: No fee listed on the official page.

properties.name: Simpson-Reed Trail
properties.description: The easiest old-growth walk in the north of the parks: a level 0.8-mile loop on a wide compacted gravel path past huge redwoods, nurse logs, ferns and a creek, with interpretive panels. The connecting Peterson Memorial loop adds about half a mile.
properties.access_notes: NPS: 'ADA accessible trail made of aggregate gravel that is four to five feet wide'; accessible parking and a non-flush accessible restroom off Walker Road; State Parks lists grades generally under 5%.
properties.source_note: Summarised from the official website; not a site visit.
properties.address: Walker Road, 0.1 mile north of US 199 (sharp, easy-to-miss turn between Crescent City and Hiouchi), Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park
properties.hours_note: Year round, daytime.
properties.geo_source: OpenStreetMap feature 'Simpson-Reed Grove Trail' (path) in our basemap tiles

trail_info.warnings: Limited parking; no RV or trailer parking. Pets not allowed.

properties.description: The Forest Service office and visitor center for the Smith River National Recreation Area on US 199 in Gasquet, offering information services, free maps and brochures, souvenirs and campfire permits. It is the place to ask about river access, swimming holes and trail conditions along the undammed Smith River.

properties.description: A mobile early-literacy programme that travels around Del Norte County offering story time, music and movement, crafts and play for children aged 0-6 and their caregivers. properties.name: Tolowa Dunes State Park
properties.description: A large coastal park of dunes, wetlands, forest and ocean beach between Crescent City and the Smith River mouth, with many miles of hiking, biking and horse trails and a long undeveloped beach. From US 101 take Northcrest Drive north (it becomes Lake Earl Drive), turn left on Lower Lake Road and go west on Kellogg Road to reach the beach area.
properties.access_notes: Page links to accessibility info but states nothing specific.
properties.source_note: Summarised from the official website; not a site visit.
properties.address: Kellogg Road / Lower Lake Road area, about 2 miles north of Crescent City (park office: 1111 Second Street, Crescent City, CA 95531)
properties.hours_note: Open year-round, day use sunrise to sunset. Campground closed until further notice.
properties.cost_note: No day-use fee listed on the official page; California State Library Parks Pass accepted.
properties.geo_source: official page: Google Maps directions link on https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=430

properties.name: Trees of Mystery
properties.description: A family-owned roadside redwood attraction marked by giant Paul Bunyan and Babe statues, where one ticket covers the forest trails, the Redwood Canopy Trail of suspended bridges, the End of the Trail Native American museum and the SkyTrail gondola, an 8-10 minute ride in enclosed six-passenger cars to a ridge-top ocean view deck. The site suggests allowing at least half a day.
properties.access_notes: FAQ: 'up in our trails we are not Wheel Chair accessible'; a shuttle to SkyTrail is offered for those who cannot easily walk the trail, and the gondola cars are described as handicapped accessible.
properties.source_note: Summarised from the official website; not a site visit.
properties.address: 15500 US-101, Klamath, CA 95548
properties.hours_note: Trail entrance 9:00 am-4:00 pm, museum 9-5, gift shop 9-5:30; open every day except Thanksgiving and Christmas, half day Christmas Eve. Call for changes.
properties.cost_note: General (13-59) $30; seniors $25; kids 3-12 $15; 0-2 free. Everything included with admission.

properties.name: Yurok Loop Trail
properties.description: An easy one-mile coastal loop (1.25 miles in the 2026 guide) from the Lagoon Creek picnic area through coastal forest and wildflowers to bluff views of sea stacks and seabirds, about ten minutes' walk from the car to the first viewpoint. The first half mile doubles as the Coastal Trail, which continues 4 miles south to the Klamath River Overlook.
properties.access_notes: 2026 park guide hike table marks 'Accessible? No'; trail is unpaved. Accessible restrooms at the Lagoon Creek lot.
properties.source_note: Summarised from the official website; not a site visit.
properties.address: Trailhead on the ocean (west) side of the Lagoon Creek day-use parking lot, signed turnoff on US 101 halfway between Crescent City and Klamath
properties.hours_note: Not listed.
